Title: Glioma-derived versican promotes tumor expansion via glioma-associated microglial/macrophages Toll-like receptor 2 signaling.

Journal/Date: Neuro-oncology (2015)

--- ABSTRACT ---
[BACKGROUND]: Accumulation and infiltration of microglia/brain macrophages around and into glioma tissue promote tumor invasion and expansion. One tumor-promoting mechanism of microglia/brain macrophages is upregulation of membrane type 1 matrix metalloprotease (MT1-MMP), which promotes the degradation of extracellular matrix. MT1-MMP upregulation is induced by soluble factors released by glioma cells activating microglial Toll-like receptor 2 (TLR2).
[METHODS]: Versican identified by proteomics was silenced in glioma cells by short interference RNA and short hairpin RNA approaches and studied in vitro and after injection into mouse brains or organotypic brain slices.
[RESULTS]: The splice variants V0/V1 of the endogenous TLR2 ligand versican are highly expressed in mouse and human glioma tissue. Versican-silenced gliomas induced less MT1-MMP expression in microglia both in vitro and in vivo, which resulted in smaller tumors and longer survival rates as compared with controls. Recombinant versican V1 induced significantly higher levels of MT1-MMP in wild-type microglia compared with untreated and treated TLR2 knockout microglial cells. Using glioma-injected organotypic brain slices, we found that the impact of versican signaling on glioma growth depended on the presence of microglia. Moreover, we found that TLR2 expression is upregulated in glioma-associated microglia but not in astrocytes. Additionally, an established TLR2 neutralizing antibody reduced glioma-induced microglial MT1-MMP expression as well as glioma growth ex vivo.
[CONCLUSIONS]: Our results show that versican released from glioma promotes tumor expansion through glioma-associated microglial/macrophage TLR2 signaling and subsequent expression of MT1-MMP. This signaling cascade might be a novel target for glioma therapies.

Title: Hyaluronan regulation of vascular integrity.
Source: American journal of cardiovascular disease (2011)
Abstract: Vascular integrity or the maintenance of blood vessel continuity is a fundamental process regulated, in part, by the endothelial glycocalyx and cell-cell junctions. Defects in endothelial barrier function are an initiating factor in several disease processes including atherosclerosis, ischemia/reperfusion, tumor angiogenesis, cancer metastasis, diabetes, sepsis and acute lung injury. The glycosaminoglycan, hyaluronan (HA), maintains vascular integrity through endothelial glycocalyx modulation, caveolin-enriched microdomain regulation and interaction with endothelial HA binding proteins. Certain disease states increase hyaluronidase activity and reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation which break down high molecular weight HA to low molecular weight fragments causing damage to the endothelial glycocalyx. Further, these HA fragments can activate specific HA binding proteins upregulated in vascular disease to promote actin cytoskeletal reorganization and inhibition of endothelial cell-cell contacts. This review focuses on the crucial role of HA in vascular integrity and how HA degradation promotes vascular barrier disruption.

Title: Toll-like receptor 2 mediates microglia/brain macrophage MT1-MMP expression and glioma expansion.

Journal/Date: Neuro-oncology (2013)

--- ABSTRACT ---
[BACKGROUND]: Glioblastomas are the most aggressive primary brain tumors in humans. Microglia/brain macrophage accumulation in and around the tumor correlates with malignancy and poor clinical prognosis of these tumors. We have previously shown that microglia promote glioma expansion through upregulation of membrane type 1 matrix metalloprotease (MT1-MMP). This upregulation depends on signaling via the Toll-like receptor (TLR) adaptor molecule myeloid differentiation primary response gene 88 (MyD88).
[METHODS]: Using in vitro, ex vivo, and in vivo techniques, we identified TLR2 as the main TLR controlling microglial MT1-MMP expression and promoting microglia-assisted glioma expansion.
[RESULTS]: The implantation of mouse GL261 glioma cells into TLR2 knockout mice resulted in significantly smaller tumors, reduced MT1-MMP expression, and enhanced survival rates compared with wild-type control mice. Tumor expansion studied in organotypic brain slices depended on both parenchymal TLR2 expression and the presence of microglia. Glioma-derived soluble factors and synthetic TLR2 specific ligands induced MT1-MMP expression in microglia from wild-type mice, but no such change in MT1-MMP gene expression was observed in microglia from TLR2 knockout mice. We also found evidence that TLR1 and TLR6 cofunction with TLR2 as heterodimers in regulating MT1-MMP expression in vitro.
[CONCLUSIONS]: Our results thus show that activation of TLR2 along with TLRs 1 and/or 6 converts microglia into a glioma supportive phenotype.

[BACKGROUND]: Accumulation and infiltration of microglia/brain macrophages around and into glioma tissue promote tumor invasion and expansion. One tumor-promoting mechanism of microglia/brain macrophages is upregulation of membrane type 1 matrix metalloprotease (MT1-MMP), which promotes the degradation of extracellular matrix. Recombinant versican V1 induced significantly higher levels of MT1-MMP in wild-type microglia compared with untreated and treated TLR2 knockout microglial cells. Using glioma-injected organotypic brain slices, we found that the impact of versican signaling on glioma growth depended on the presence of microglia. Moreover, we found that TLR2 expression is upregulated in glioma-associated microglia but not in astrocytes. Additionally, an established TLR2 neutralizing antibody reduced glioma-induced microglial MT1-MMP expression as well as glioma growth ex vivo.
[CONCLUSIONS]: Our results show that versican released from glioma promotes tumor expansion through glioma-associated microglial/macrophage TLR2 signaling and subsequent expression of MT1-MMP. This signaling cascade might be a novel target for glioma therapies.

key_findings.finding: The central primary study supports the proposition: glioma-derived versican (VCAN), specifically V0/V1 isoforms, promotes glioma expansion through TLR2 signaling in glioma-associated microglia/brain macrophages. In PMID 25452390 (Neuro-Oncology, 2015; title: “Glioma-derived versican promotes tumor expansion via glioma-associated microglial/macrophages Toll-like receptor 2 signaling”), VCAN was identified by proteomics, was highly expressed in mouse and human glioma tissue, and was reduced in glioma cells using siRNA/shRNA. VCAN-silenced tumors induced less microglial MT1-MMP, formed smaller intracerebral tumors, and prolonged mouse survival; the effect on growth in organotypic brain slices required microglia.

source_tools.relevance: Independent focused search identifying the primary study

key_findings.finding: The study provides both genetic and pharmacologic evidence for TLR2 mediation. Recombinant VCAN V1 induced MT1-MMP in wild-type microglia but not TLR2-knockout microglia; TLR2 expression was increased in glioma-associated microglia but not astrocytes; and a TLR2-neutralizing antibody reduced glioma-induced microglial MT1-MMP and ex vivo glioma growth. Thus, the proposed pathway is VCAN→TLR2 on glioma-associated microglia/brain macrophages→MT1-MMP→tumor expansion.

source_tools.relevance: Primary-study abstract with knockout and neutralizing-antibody evidence

key_findings.finding: A preceding mechanistic primary study, PMID 24014382 (Neuro-Oncology, 2013; “Toll-like receptor 2 mediates microglia/brain macrophage MT1-MMP expression and glioma expansion”), established that TLR2 is functionally required for microglia-assisted glioma growth: GL261 implantation into TLR2-knockout mice produced smaller tumors, lower MT1-MMP, and longer survival than wild-type controls; organotypic growth required parenchymal TLR2 and microglia; glioma-derived soluble factors induced MT1-MMP in wild-type but not TLR2-knockout microglia. It also implicated TLR1/TLR6 heterodimerization with TLR2.

Important limitations/qualifications: the VCAN-specific evidence is centered on one main primary study (PMID 25452390), and the accessible record is only the abstract; detailed cell-line identities, dosing, isoform-specific loss-of-function controls, and full statistical/methodological details could not be verified here. The causal tumor-growth experiments are mainly mouse intracerebral implants and organotypic brain-slice/ex vivo systems, while human evidence is primarily tissue expression. The experiments emphasize resident microglia/brain macrophages and MT1-MMP as the effector; they do not establish that all human glioma-associated monocyte-derived macrophages respond identically. No directly contradictory primary study was identified in the searches, but the evidence does not by itself prove that VCAN-TLR2 is the only glioma-to-myeloid growth pathway or that it is clinically dominant in patients.
